# Review

## Summary

The bridge adds a second durable receipt (`isolated.json`) that is written **only** after `inspect()` revalidates the exact live container policy (image ID, no mounts, NetworkMode none, ReadonlyRootfs, no privilege, CapDrop ALL, fixed working dir, nonce/spec labels), and `captureQuiescence` then requires **both** receipts plus a fresh daemon-ID/Linux/404 confirmation before returning frozen per-invocation refs.

**isolation** — Pass. `recordIsolation` runs only post-inspect; `durable()` uses atomic no-replace link + fsync; `isolation()` re-reads via `O_NOFOLLOW`/`fstat` bounded read, strict schema, exact launch equality (containerId+nonce+specDigest+daemonId) and policy-digest recomputation. Missing, symlinked, oversized, policy-tampered, launch-swapped, and future receipts all fail before any daemon call (tested). Legacy removed invocations without `isolated.json` fail closed and cannot be retrofitted (`confirmStopped` does not create receipts; `stop()` short-circuits on already-stopped).

**physical** — Pass. `captureQuiescence` requires the durable stop receipt bound to the same launch, then a fresh `confirmStopped` (daemon ID + OSType revalidated, exact container-ID 404), and rejects if live evidence differs from the journaled receipt. No absence/expiry/PID inference; evidence refs are hashes of the full receipts; recheck is synchronous, network-free, and detects journal drift. Trusted-daemon/admin boundary is explicitly documented and matches the task's stated threat model.

**transaction** — Pass. The reopen closure pins the complete `GraphExecutorInventory` at reopen and, inside the caller's G15 transaction, uses `assertExecutorInventory` (requires `db.inTransaction`, recomputes the full inventory digest in-place — no nested `BEGIN`, no daemon await) plus a synchronous binding-journal re-read and the executor's synchronous `proof.recheck()`. Current grants are re-authorized synchronously on every recheck; revocation, release drift, inventory/other-action drift, and receipt loss all fail closed inside the real `GraphReconciler` commit path (tested via actual `store.commit` verifier callback). Unknown business verdict is persisted with admission retained; no release occurs.

**scope** — Pass. Proof is explicitly `contained-invocation` scoped; sweep and reopen APIs do not infer graph-wide quiescence; opaque adapters remain unproven (`addOpaque` drift test); no RPC, replay, auto-release, or takeover added; general cancel/takeover remains TODO as stated.

**Non-blocking observations** (warnings, not failures against the stated criteria):
- Deterministic evidence notes real Docker/Loop daemon tests are still pending; all coverage here is fixture/mock-daemon based. The "actual G15 integration test" uses a mocked daemon boundary, so end-to-end Docker inspect/DELETE behavior against a real daemon remains unverified.
- Residual TOCTOU between `realpathSync` directory validation and the subsequent `O_NOFOLLOW` file open (directory components could be swapped by an actor already inside the trusted host-journal boundary). Accepted by the stated trust model.
- The deterministic log notes one test correction mid-run ("stale revision after successful G15 commit"); the corrected expectation is reasonable but the initial failure is only summarized, not shown.

All four evaluation criteria pass on the supplied evidence; no blocking findings. Approved with advisory follow-ups.

# Review

The contained proof bridge persists a separate isolation receipt only after exact Docker inspect validates the live container policy, and captureQuiescence requires both durable receipts plus a fresh exact-daemon Linux/404 confirmation before returning frozen per-invocation refs with a synchronous, network-free recheck. Receipt tamper/swap/missing/future/symlink/oversize cases all fail closed before daemon access; legacy stopped receipts without isolation cannot be retrofitted. The G15 final-transaction closure re-checks current synchronous grants, the complete pinned GraphExecutorInventory (no nested transaction, no daemon await), and the binding journal; drift or revocation fails closed with the unknown business verdict preserved and admission held. Scope stays strictly per-invocation; no RPC, replay, release, or takeover authority added. Advisory: real Docker/Loop integration remains pending (fixture-only evidence) and a bounded directory-component TOCTOU exists inside the trusted host-journal boundary.

captureQuiescence first requires both durable receipts bound to the same launch, then performs a fresh confirmStopped with daemon-ID/OSType revalidation and exact container-ID 404, rejecting any mismatch with journaled evidence; no absence/expiry/PID inference, exact-ID-only deletion, immutable frozen refs, and a synchronous network-free recheck under the explicitly documented trusted daemon/admin boundary.

The returned closure requires db.inTransaction, re-authorizes current synchronous grants, asserts the complete pinned GraphExecutorInventory in-place (no nested BEGIN, no daemon await), re-reads the binding journal, and runs the executor's synchronous proof recheck; grant revocation, admission release drift, inventory/other-action changes, and receipt loss all fail closed inside the actual GraphReconciler G15 commit, with unknown verdict persisted and no release.

Proof is explicitly scoped 'contained-invocation', cannot authorize graph recovery, sweep/reopen paths do not infer graph-wide quiescence, opaque-adapter actions remain unproven, legacy stopped receipts without isolation stay unproven, and no public RPC, business verdict, auto replay/release/takeover was added; general cancel/takeover remains documented TODO.

findings.message: Residual TOCTOU between realpathSync directory validation and the O_NOFOLLOW file open: an actor able to swap directory components inside the trusted host-journal root could race the read. Within the stated trusted host-journal boundary, but worth a future hardening note (e.g., dirfd-relative opens).
findings.evidence: directory() checks realpathSync(dir) !== dir, then read() opens join(dir, name) as a fresh path lookup.

findings.message: One recovery test expectation was corrected mid-run for a stale revision read after successful G15 commit; the correction is consistent with the commit advancing revision, but the original failing assertion is only summarized in the evidence.
findings.evidence: Deterministic results summary: '66 tests pass after correcting a test read with stale revision after successful G15 commit; initial 65pass/1fail preserved.'

recommended_actions: Run the pending real Docker/Loop integration tests against the dedicated pinned Linux daemon to validate inspect/DELETE/404 behavior end-to-end before relying on the bridge outside fixtures.
Consider dirfd-relative (openat-style) reads for journal files to eliminate the residual directory-component swap race within the trusted journal root.
